cameras.hasTelemetryHelper: Tick this only for cameras that really move. Firmware advertises the ONVIF PTZ service whether or not there is a motor behind it, so the joystick and object tracking are gated on this switch, not on what the camera claims. The camera's ONVIF settings page still shows what it reports — check there first.

cameras.roiTranscodeHint: Re-encodes finished clips, keeping detected objects sharp and compressing the rest harder. Only clips that have detection boxes are touched.
cameras.roiDelayHoursHint: 0 re-compresses as soon as the clip is closed and its detections are stored. Fractional values are allowed.
cameras.roiCoverageHint: Coverage is the share of a clip's length that has detection boxes on it. Only clips inside this band are re-compressed: below it the detector saw too little to trust, above it there is no background left to squeeze. 0 turns a bound off.

tracking.selfGuidanceHint: The camera picks a target and moves by itself, around the clock, whether or not anyone is watching. Detections drive it, so raise this camera’s analytics sample rate above 1 fps or the movement will be jerky.
tracking.prioritiesHint: In order: the first of these in the picture is the one followed.
tracking.anyObject: Nothing chosen — any object will do.
tracking.sourcesHint: Only boxes from the checked producers are followed.
tracking.anySource: Nothing chosen — boxes from either producer will do.
tracking.releaseTooltip: Release this object and go back to the camera’s own priorities
tracking.startTooltip: Start following objects on this camera
tracking.notRunning: Following is switched on, but this camera cannot be driven
tracking.selfGuidanceSlaveHint: This camera is aimed at objects seen by “{{master}}”, through the survey marked out under “Follow a master camera”. It does not look for objects in its own picture. Switching this on starts it moving, around the clock.
tracking.uncalibrated: Not calibrated. Tracking still works: it assumes the camera is hung the usual way — panning right slides the picture left. If the camera moves away from the object instead of towards it, one of its axes is reversed and the Calibration tab will fix it.
tracking.calibrated: Calibrated ({{method}}), so the camera knows which way its own motor turns.
tracking.slaveNeedsWholeObjects: Faces and licence plates cannot aim this camera. A slave is pointed by reading the bottom edge of a box as the spot where the object stands, and a face's bottom edge is a chin — so it is skipped, and the camera follows the body it belongs to instead. Put “person” or “vehicle” on the list, or nothing will move when only a face is seen.
tracking.masterTooltip: Cameras are aimed by this one's picture. Switch boxes on and click an object to point them at it.
tracking.masterReleaseTooltip: Release the object and let the cameras aimed by this one choose again

slaveBinding.title: Follow a master camera
slaveBinding.intro: A stationary camera with analytics finds the objects; this camera is pointed at them. There are no geo-coordinates, so the pair is tied together by spots you mark by hand — a place in the master's picture, and where this camera was looking at the time.
slaveBinding.methodAbsoluteHint: Interpolates between the marked spots, so the camera can be sent anywhere between them. Needs a camera that really executes AbsoluteMove — some accept the command and ignore it, so check with “Go here” before trusting it.
slaveBinding.methodPresetsHint: Drives to the preset of the nearest marked spot. Coarser, and the only thing that works on a camera whose absolute positioning is a stub.
slaveBinding.masterHasNoStream: The chosen master has no WebRTC stream, so there is no picture to mark spots on.
slaveBinding.pickHint: Click the master's picture where the ground is — where an object's feet would be. Mark spots around the perimeter of the working area rather than all in one corner. Drag a marker to move it.
slaveBinding.driveHint: Drive this camera until the marked spot sits on the crosshair. Aim about a person's height above the spot on the ground rather than at the ground itself: the mapping then carries that framing correction, its own at every distance, while still taking the ground as its input.
slaveBinding.residualHint: The number beside a spot is how far the rest of the survey lands from it when it is left out — so the largest one is where to look first for a mis-marked spot. One bad spot raises its neighbours' numbers too; fix the worst and the rest settle.
slaveBinding.residualTooltip: How far the other marked spots say this one should be
slaveBinding.goHere: Send the camera to this spot
slaveBinding.needPresets: {{count}} of {{total}} marked spots have no preset, so part of the master's picture has nothing to aim at.
slaveBinding.needPositions: Coordinates need at least 3 marked spots whose position could be read; there are {{count}}.
slaveBinding.aimedOutside: Sent to {{where}} — outside the marked area, so this is the mapping continuing rather than interpolating.
slaveBinding.nothingToRecord: This camera would not report its position and no preset was chosen, so there is nothing to record.
slaveBinding.aimFailed: Could not send the camera there.
slaveBinding.slaveHasNoStream: This camera has no WebRTC stream, so its picture cannot be shown here. Drive it with the pad below and watch it wherever you normally do.
slaveBinding.zonesHint: The shading is the aiming rule itself: each colour is the part of the master's view from which its marked spot is the nearest, so that is the preset the slave gets sent to. There is no radius — every part of the picture belongs to some spot. Uncoloured patches belong to a spot with no preset, where the slave has nowhere to go.
slaveBinding.cameraPresetsHint: The slave's own stored positions. A preset's name says nothing about where it points, so click one to send the camera there and look. Deleting one also unpins any marked spot that was using it — the spot stays, with nothing to aim at, which is what the survey should show.
slaveBinding.deletePreset: Delete this preset from the camera
slaveBinding.gotoFailed: Could not send the camera to that preset.
slaveBinding.savedAsYouGo: Changes are saved as you make them.
slaveBinding.updatePreset: Re-record this preset where the camera is pointing now, keeping its name. Drive the camera first, then press this.
slaveBinding.presetUpdated: “{{name}}” now points where the camera is.
slaveBinding.presetCopied: The camera stored a new preset ({{token}}) instead of replacing “{{name}}”. Marked spots were re-pinned to the new one, so the survey still works; the old entry is still on the camera and can be deleted from this list.
